How it is calculated
That looked like touchpad or touch input. These tools measure a mouse, so plug one in or connect it over Bluetooth. Press Escape to stop.
Polling rate tester
See how many times per second your mouse reports its position. Click the box, then move the mouse in fast circles.
Click to start. Your cursor is captured while measuring.
%1$s reports · Esc or right-click to stop
Current
Average
Peak
Reset
Closest standard rate: %1$s Hz
Each report is timed by the kernel when the mouse sends it, so this reads the real rate rather than the screen refresh rate. Fast circles work best.
Every mouse report carries a timestamp. The tool measures the gap between consecutive reports and ignores gaps over %1$d ms, which are pauses in your movement.

Average is the number of gaps divided by the time they add up to. Current uses the last quarter second of movement, and peak is the highest of those readings so far. Averaging over time keeps bursts of reports with near-identical timestamps from inflating them.
Mouse rotation
Check whether your side to side swipes are really horizontal with your natural grip, then get an angle to correct it.
1. Click inside the box to start. Your cursor is captured while measuring.
2. Swipe the mouse side to side at least %1$d times.
3. Right-click or press Escape to stop and see the result.
Right-click or press Escape to stop and see the result.
Click to start
Measuring: %1$d swipes
Click to restart
Recommended rotation
Only %1$d swipes counted. Swipe at least %2$d times and try again.
Margin of error ±%1$s° over %2$d swipes. More swipes narrow it.

Positive angles rotate the sensor output clockwise. Vendors differ on sign, so test with a few swipes after you apply it. Movement is read as raw sensor counts, without Android\'s pointer acceleration.
While you measure, every mouse report gives a small move (dx, dy). Each swipe is reduced to its net movement, and the tool adds up dx², dy² and dx·dy across the swipes.
θ = ½ · atan2(2 · Σ dx·dy, Σ dx² − Σ dy²)

Those three sums give the direction your swipes line up with: the straight line that sits closest to all your movements. Because the sums use squares and products, swiping left and right gives the same answer as swiping one way.
The recommended rotation is that line\'s angle from horizontal, rounded to one decimal. A swipe is counted when you reverse direction after a clear stroke, so small jitters don\'t add to the total.
